vegetation:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: high-resolution transparent sprite atlas for an overhead fantasy settlement map. Produce ONE square atlas containing EXACTLY 36 separate botanical brush stamps in a precise 6-column by 6-row equal-cell grid. No labels, text, outlines of cells, or ground tiles.
Style: delicately hand-painted watercolor and fine botanical ink, natural muted olive and sage greens, warm earthy highlights, detailed readable foliage rather than simple geometric circles. STRICT vertical overhead orthographic view, showing the top of canopies, not side-view or isometric trees. Soft subtle directional shading contained within each canopy, no long cast shadow. Each stamp isolated on actual transparent alpha, centered in its cell; keep all foliage within the central 65% of that cell so generous completely transparent gutters separate all stamps.
Row 1 TEMPERATE, columns 1–6: mature lobed oak canopy; rounded apple tree canopy; light birch canopy; spreading elm canopy; flowering shrub; low hawthorn bush.
Row 2 FOREST, columns 1–6: spruce star-shaped canopy; layered Scots pine canopy; silver fir canopy; dense beech canopy; fern thicket; young evergreen.
Row 3 DESERT, columns 1–6: date palm fronds; branching doum palm canopy; sparse flat acacia canopy; tamarisk canopy; thorn scrub; dry golden grass tussock. No cactus.
Row 4 STEPPE, columns 1–6: sparse acacia canopy; low juniper; small hardy fruit tree; sagebrush; golden tussock grass; green wild grass and tiny flowers.
Row 5 TROPICAL, columns 1–6: coconut palm fronds; dense large broadleaf canopy; banana leaf clump; giant fern; flowering tropical shrub; irregular jungle canopy.
Row 6 TUNDRA, columns 1–6: dwarf willow shrub; low dwarf birch; compact juniper; heather cushion; sedge tussock; pale lichen cushion.
All 36 stamps distinct, coherent scale within plant class, clean alpha edges with no opaque rectangular background, no checkerboard painted in the image, no horizon, no pots, no people or buildings. Rendering atlas for a real app, not a presentation. Square composition, highest practical resolution.

terrain:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent overhead natural terrain and cultivation brush-stamp atlas for an antique fantasy settlement map, companion to botanical canopy stamps.
Produce ONE square high-resolution atlas of EXACTLY 36 distinct stamps in a perfect 6-column by 6-row equal-cell grid. All contents centered WITHIN the central 60% of EACH cell, generous completely transparent gutters, no stamp touching its neighbors or the outside edges. Actual transparent alpha background, no opaque square tiles, no printed checkerboard, no grid or text.
Art: delicate hand-painted watercolor with crisp fine natural detail, subtle shade and highlight, muted ochre/sage/earth palette compatible with parchment cartography. STRICT vertical orthographic overhead view, not horizon landscape, not isometric. Each stamp a small irregular independent land-detail cluster fading organically to transparent edges. No large cast shadows, no colorful edge halos.
Row1 DUNES: six varied small wind-shaped sand dune clusters seen from overhead, gentle ochre ridges and shaded slipfaces, a crescent dune, paired curved dunes, soft linear dunes, low rippled sand, a tiny dune crescent, irregular sand ridges. Transparent outside actual dune cluster, no background sand rectangle.
Row2 ROCKS: six varied modest grey/brown rock clusters with different numbers and sizes, rocky gravel and a low outcrop, overhead.
Row3 GRASS: six mixed grass-and-wildflower tussocks of green/olive/golden shades, low fern/meadow details, no trees.
Row4 WETLAND: six reeds/sedges/wetland vegetation clumps with tiny dark green moss, no painted water tile or standing blue water.
Row5 GARDENS: six small clusters of vegetable plant rosettes/leafy seedlings/herbs with a little dark earthy detail, overhead, no rectangular garden boundary and no walls.
Row6 CROPS: six small wheat/barley/oat/green crop clusters with gently parallel plant rows, warm golden or olive shades, no rectangular field boundary, no ground tile.
These are stamps to mix across real procedurally placed map fields, gardens and land patches; never draw buildings, roads, labels, fences, or full landscape scenes. Coherent crisp botanical detail, each stamp fully isolated and readable at zoom. Square composition with the six row categories exactly as listed.
